conviction_note: TEN's own disclosed rate sensitivity (+$0.13 annual EPS per $1,000/day) applied to the verified Q1->Q2 2026 sequential spot step-up implies Q2 EPS near $3.2-3.7 against a two-analyst consensus of $2.48 that models a sequential DECLINE, but TEN demonstrably does not re-rate on EPS (it fell 1.62% on a ~100% Q1 beat), so I size the beat at roughly the median historical reaction and net off drydock drag and the absence of a dividend at this seasonal slot.

findings.finding: The only published Q2 preview has consensus at $2.48 EPS / $220.6m revenue from TWO analysts — a sequential decline from Q1's $2.72 on $253.0m gross revenue — while Teekay's audited Q2 comparatives show mid-size spot TCE rose sequentially by $47,047/day (Suezmax $62,124 -> $109,171) and $14,215/day (Aframax/LR2 $59,934 -> $74,149); TEN told the market on its Q1 call that 37% of the operating fleet is market-exposed and that every $1,000/day of spot rate is worth $0.13 of ANNUAL EPS, which arithmetic puts Q2 EPS near $3.2-3.7, a 30-50% beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is two analysts, and the same two were 30-100% below on Q1 ($2.72 actual against $1.35 on the same wire and $2.07 elsewhere). There is no options market to arbitrage it away: total open interest is 7,566 contracts on a $1.3bn cap and the ATM spread is 100% of mid, and short interest is 0.7% of shares at 1.0 day to cover, so nobody has taken a position either way. If this were priced the preview would not be asking 'was Q1 peak earnings' and the mean target would not sit at $46, 6% above spot, on a name the same note calls the cheapest crude tanker at 0.38x P/NAV and 2.6x forward P/E.
findings.independence: Teekay's Q2 rate comparatives are from a different filer's own SEC release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1419945/000141994526000054/tnkq2-26erdocument.htm (2026-07-29). TEN's $0.13/$1,000 sensitivity and the 37% market-exposed figure are from the Q1 call transcript, a separate document: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-tsakos-energy-navigation-q1-2026-earnings-soar-93CH-4704494 (2026-05-21).

findings.finding: TEN's own 2026 drydocking plan, given only on the Q4 2025 call, front-loads maintenance into exactly the record-rate quarters: two vessels in Q1, FIVE in Q2 and SEVEN in Q3 against three in Q4 — so Q1's 98.3% utilisation is the easy comparison and Q3 off-hire will be taken with VLCC and Suezmax spot at or near all-time highs.
findings.why_not_priced: It was said once, on a March call, and appears in no preview, no wire copy and no sell-side note I could find; the two covering analysts are modelling a revenue number ($220.6m) below the last reported quarter, which is not a drydock-adjusted forecast, it is a stale one. If the drydock cadence were in the price the Q3 guidance question would be framed as an off-hire question rather than a 'have rates peaked' question.
findings.independence: None found from a second source — this rests on one transcript. It is the direct offset to finding 1 and cuts against it, which is why I have kept both small rather than netting them out.

findings.finding: This print will carry no common dividend: TEN's own H1 2025 release said the semi-annual payment 'is intended to be announced in November', and the declaration record confirms the pattern — ex-dates Jul 2024, Dec 2024, Jul 2025, Dec 2025, Feb 2026, Jul 2026 and nothing in September in any year — while TEN has already declared its full $1.50 for 2026 ($0.50 paid February, $1.00 paid July).
findings.why_not_priced: TEN is a yield-owned Greek tanker name whose last two positive earnings reactions (+3.29% on 2025-06-25 and +4.83% on 2024-12-03) both coincided with dividend declarations, and the sweep brief that commissioned this hunt itself assumed 'the dividend decision routinely dominates the earnings line' at this print. If the absence were understood, the run-in would not look like a dividend run-in. The counter-case, and why the band crosses zero, is that record H1 cash plus the >$100m released by the 1 September Suezmax sales gives the board room for a surprise third 2026 declaration.
findings.independence: Declaration and ex-date history from a separate source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ten/dividend/ (retrieved 2026-09-09). The >$100m of sale proceeds is from the company release https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/01/3354219/0/en/ten-ltd-announces-sale-of-two-first-generation-suezmax-tankers.html (2026-09-01).

findings.finding: Live Baltic assessments for the week to 4 September 2026 have VLCC TD3C at WS677.22 and rising (round-trip TCE near $704,000/day) and Suezmax TD6 at ~$180,500/day, which directly contradicts the only published preview's framing that 'recent diplomatic efforts and some easing of transit restrictions' put the cycle in doubt — TEN's H1 release conventionally carries Q3-to-date and forward-booking commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Only weakly unpriced, which is why it is sized at 0.3: the tanker tape is public and the sector is at highs. What is unpriced is the specific mismatch between the sell-side framing published the day before the print and the tape published five days before it. Shares the 'rates are strong' theme with finding 1 and should be collapsed with it if the scorer clusters by theme.
findings.independence: Same directional theme as finding 1 but a different period (Q3-to-date rather than reported Q2) and a different document. Corroborated by a separate trade report: https://www.lloydslist.com/LL1156492/Crude-tanker-rates-in-unchartered-territory-VLCC-index-tops-420K

findings.finding: TEN's insiders now file Section 16 forms — a mass of Form 3s on 2026-03-18 followed by Form 4s — and two independent directors each halved their direct stake into the run-up: Nicholas Tommasino sold 2,490 of 5,364 shares at $40.065 on 2026-07-14 and Clio Hatzimichalis sold 5,000 of 10,000 at $41.0662 on 2026-08-13; separately CEO Nikolaos Tsakos moved 500,000 shares to his spouse at $0 on 2026-07-08.
findings.why_not_priced: Foreign private issuers are exempt from Section 16, so TEN has historically appeared in no insider-transaction screen and no aggregator tracks it; the filings began only in March 2026. But I am sizing this near zero deliberately: the two sales total roughly $300k against a $1.3bn market cap, and the CEO transfer is a $0 estate transfer, not a sale. It is a 'nobody is looking here' item whose content is trivial.
findings.independence: Second director sale is a separate filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166663/000119312526306135/ownership.xml (2026-07-16), with a matching Form 144 notice of proposed sale filed 2026-07-14.

searched_and_found_nothing: The sweep's headline thesis — that TEN's high time-charter cover means it under-converts the spot spike and will disappoint a peer read-across — did not survive contact with the disclosure. TEN's profit-sharing is geared, not absent: Q1 2026 profit-share revenue alone exceeded $40m against roughly $45m for the whole of 2025, and management told the Q1 call it expected Q2 to be stronger than Q1. The 84.7% TC cover figure is real (Nortilus, 2026-07-22) but it coexists with 37% of the operating fleet carrying market exposure through spot and profit-share.
Dividend surprise as the main catalyst: ruled out by the September seasonal pattern rather than confirmed.
Preferred redemption: Series E is fixed to 5/28/2027 and Series F to 7/30/2028, neither callable now, so no near-term common-EPS uplift from redemption.
Short squeeze / positioning: short interest 204,453 shares (0.7% of stock), 1.0 day to cover as of 2026-08-14. No mechanism.

Equity issuance risk from the F-3ASR filed 2026-07-02: it registers an unspecified amount of debt, preferred and common, but with $2.0bn of remaining newbuild capex funded to date by secured debt and asset sales, and the stock at 0.38x NAV, I could find no evidence of a pending takedown. Treated as routine three-year shelf renewal.
Customer/charterer distress on the shuttle-tanker book (Petrobras/Brazil exposure) — nothing found.
Any 6-K between 2026-05-22 and today: EDGAR shows none, so the results release will be the first substantive filing in nearly four months.

Note for the record: the baseline dates TEN's H1 2025 print 2025-09-30 and tags it amc; the company's own H1 2025 release is dated 2025-09-10, pre-open, so that historical reaction is measured on the wrong session and the 1.62% median rests partly on mis-anchored data.
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline on both counts — my net is positive while the +10.5 25-delta skew says downside is being paid and the stock is already +14.1% over twenty sessions and 1.9% off its high — but the skew is drawn from a chain with 7,566 total contracts of open interest and a 100%-of-mid ATM spread, which is a quote artefact rather than a positioning statement, and the run-up is a sector rally on a name still at 2.6x forward earnings, so neither is the constraint on this print; the real constraint is that TEN has never re-rated on an earnings beat, which is why the number is 1.3 and not 4.
